\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.Pseudorandomness.CorrelationImmunity}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Correlation immunity]
\lean{FABL.IsCorrelationImmune}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p170-b002
}
\label{FABL.IsCorrelationImmune}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and a natural number $k$,
correlation immunity is the property that the real-valued version of $f$ is Fourier
regular with parameters $0$ and $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Resilience]
\lean{FABL.IsResilient}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p170-b002
}
\label{FABL.IsResilient}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.IsCorrelationImmune}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and a natural number $k$,
resilience means that $f$ is correlation immune with parameter $k$ and that its
real-valued version is balanced.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Correlation immunity of a parity function]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_isCorrelationImmune}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b007
}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_isCorrelationImmune}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsCorrelationImmune, FABL.fourierCoeff_monomial, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $k$ be
a natural number. If $|S|=k+1$, then every nonempty coordinate set of size at most $k$
has Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most zero for the real-valued parity
function associated to $S$; equivalently, all such coefficients vanish.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Balance of a nonempty parity function]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_isBalanced}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b007
}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_isBalanced}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.mean, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a nonempty subset of the $n$ coordinates. The
real-valued parity function associated to $S$ has mean zero on the sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Resilience of parity]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction_isResilient}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b007
}
\label{FABL.parityFunction_isResilient}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsResilient, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_isBalanced, FABL.parityFunction_isCorrelationImmune}
\difficulty{3}
Let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, let $k$ be a natural number, and suppose
$|S|=k+1$. The parity function on $S$ is resilient of order $k$: it is balanced, and
every nonempty Fourier coefficient indexed by a set of at most $k$ coordinates is zero.
\end{theorem}
